theme: repository preservation and public asset review
question: Can the research repository be made public while preserving frozen local evidence and excluding unresolved-rights payloads and access artifacts?
outcome: Filtered exactly two local-only source/access paths from the two published branch histories. The final screen checked 14,465 blobs, with zero known credential/signed-URL matches, forbidden paths or oversized blobs. A pristine checkout passed 983 Markdown documents, 50 catalogue manifest hashes and 362 drawing paths. GitHub public visibility and anonymous commit/README access were verified.
challenge: A mixed comparison retained full Lipi sequences and an access record contained a signed download URL. Nested Windows paths caused false file/link omissions; a concurrent working README edit affected the first anonymous-content comparison.
remedy: Keep original local bytes, private all-ref bundles and selected-working-tree backup. Filter only exact paths in an isolated mirror, correct Windows path handling without editing frozen evidence, verify a pristine checkout, use an atomic two-branch push with explicit leases, and check anonymous access against the immutable publication commit.
retry_when: Any newly acquired or copied source material needs its own asset review; no automatic public upload of raw corpora.
